'''Ivan Paul Kaminow''' (3 March 1930 - 18 December 2013) was an American electrical engineer and scientific researcher.

== Early life and education ==

He was born on 3 March 1930 in [[Union City, New Jersey]].<ref name=PTobit>Chang-Hasnain, Connie. [https://physicstoday.aip.org/obituaries/ivan-paul-kaminow "Ivan Paul Kaminow"], ''[[Physics Today]]'', November 1, 2014. Accessed March 9, 2026. "Born on 3 March 1930 in Union City, New Jersey, Ivan received his BS in electrical engineering from Union College in 1952. After earning his MS, also in engineering, from UCLA in 1954, he began a 42-year career at Bell Labs. He earned a PhD from Harvard University in 1960; his thesis, under C. Lester Hogan and later R. Victor Jones, was on ferromagnetic resonance at microwave frequencies and high pressures."</ref> Raised in [[Passaic, New Jersey]], he graduated in 1948 from [[Passaic High School]].<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-herald-news-updates-from-passaic-are/192992789/ "Campus Corner"], ''[[Herald News]]'', March 24, 1950. Accessed March 9, 2026, via [[Newspapers.com]]. "Ivan P. Kaminow, son of Mr. and Mrs. Benjamin Kaminow, 42 Pleasant Avenue, Passaic, is on the dean's list at Union College, Schenectady, N. Y. A sophomore, he is majoring in electrical engineering. He was graduated from Passaic High School in 1948."</ref>

He completed his bachelor's degree from [[Union College (New York)|Union College]]<ref name="www2.eecs.berkeley.edu">{{Cite web |title=Ivan P. Kaminow {{!}} EECS at UC Berkeley |url=https://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Faculty/Homepages/kaminow.html |access-date=2026-03-10 |website=www2.eecs.berkeley.edu}}</ref> and earned his MS in electrical engineering, from [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in 1954.<ref name=PTobit/> He completed his PhD at [[Harvard University]],<ref name="www2.eecs.berkeley.edu"/> where his thesis was on ferromagnetic resonance at microwave frequencies and high pressures was supervised by [[C. Lester Hogan]] and later R. Victor Jones.<ref name=PTobit/>

== Career  ==
He retired from [[Bell Labs]] in 1996 after a 42-year long career lasting from 1954 to 1996, mostly in lightwave research.<ref name="www2.eecs.berkeley.edu"/>

At [[Bell Labs]], he did seminal research on electrooptic modulators and materials, Raman scattering in ferroelectrics, integrated optics (including titanium-diffused lithium niobate modulators) and semiconductor lasers.<ref name="www2.eecs.berkeley.edu"/>

== Death ==
He died in [[San Francisco]] on 18 December 2013.<ref name=PTobit/>

== Awards and honors ==
He received many awards for his contributions to photonics, including:<ref name=PTobit/>

* 1995 [[Charles Hard Townes Award]]
* 2010 Photonics Award 
* 2011 [[Frederic Ives Medal]] from the Optical Society (OSA)
* 2013 Edison Medal from the IEEE
* 1997 John Tyndall Award from IEEE/OSA.
